SAN FRANCISCO, October 29, 2026--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Reddit, Inc. (NYSE: RDDT) today announced financial results for the quarter ended September 30, 2026. Reddit's complete financial results and management commentary can be found in its shareholder letter on Reddit's Investor Relations website at https://investor.redditinc.com.

"Our business is growing because the Reddit experience captures the human experience in a way that no other platform can replicate," said Steve Huffman, Founder and CEO of Reddit. "Surpassing $3B of revenue over the last 12 months shows Reddit's strength as a destination and the differentiated value of our platform."

Strong Growth and Fundamentals

Total revenue increased 53% year-over-year to $895 million, Ad revenue increased 54% year-over-year to $847 million, and Other revenue increased 35% year-over-year to $48 million

Gross margin was 91.5%, up 50 bps year-over-year

Net income was $283 million, an improvement of $121 million from the prior year

Adjusted EBITDA1 was $402 million, an improvement of $166 million from the prior year

Basic and diluted earnings per share ("EPS") were $1.47 and $1.40, an increase of 69% and 75% year-over-year, respectively

Operating cash flow was $364 million, an improvement of $179 million from the prior year

Free Cash Flow1 was $363 million, an improvement of $179 million from the prior year

Capital expenditures were $1 million, 0.1% of revenue

Managed Share Count and Dilution

Total fully diluted shares outstanding were 206.3 million as of September 30, 2026, down 0.3% from last quarter

Solid Balance Sheet

Cash, Cash Equivalents, and Marketable Securities were $3.03 billion as of September 30, 2026

Share Repurchases

We repurchased approximately 670 thousand shares of our Class A common stock during the quarter for a total of $100 million at an average price per share of $149.81

Company Recognition

Reddit was added to the S&P 500 index, underscoring the Company's value, sustained performance, and its 1-of-1 financial model

title: Dear Reddit Stock Fans, Mark Your Calendars for October 29

Trade Reddit on Coinbase

Financial Report by NicoElNino via Shutterstock

Popular social media platform Reddit (RDDT) is set to report its third-quarter results for fiscal 2026 on Oct. 29, after the market closes. Ahead of the results, the stock has been under pressure as investors question the sustainability of its growth. Investors have raised concerns because Google Search's AI-generated answers are feared to reduce website traffic.

For the third quarter, Reddit expects revenue between $860 million and $870 million. However, the user mix has not been that special, as logged-out users are growing faster than logged-in users. Starting with the third-quarter results, the company will no longer report logged-in and logged-out daily active users separately, which might raise the question of a lack of visibility into its metrics.

Ahead of the earnings, let's take a closer look at Reddit.

About Reddit Stock

Reddit is a website where people share posts, links, pictures, and videos. Users join communities called subreddits, which focus on topics like sports, games, news, movies, or hobbies. Other users vote posts and comments up or down, helping decide which content appears first. Each subreddit has moderators who set rules and remove posts that break them.

Reddit's employees run the website, improve its technology, manage safety policies, and earn money through advertising and data licensing. The platform connects people with similar interests and lets them discuss almost any topic. It is headquartered in San Francisco, California, and has a market capitalization of $26.25 billion.

RDDT stock is down 38% over the past 52 weeks and 11% over the past six months. The company is still growing quickly and profitably, but the market is pricing in risks around Google-driven traffic and slowing growth. The stock reached a 52-week low of $119.27 on March 30 but is up 10% from that level.

On a forward-adjusted basis, Reddit's price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio of 25.29x is higher than the industry average of 14.21x.

www.barchart.com
Strong Second-Quarter Results

With ad revenue up 64% year-over-year (YoY) to $762 million (driven by higher pricing and impressions), Reddit's second-quarter revenue climbed 61% YoY to $805 million. The company crossed $1 million in revenue per employee. This also marked the eighth consecutive quarter of more than 60% YoY growth. The results also indicated that Reddit's international segment is growing faster than the U.S. segment.

Shares of Meta Platforms (META) fell 19.7% from October 13 to October 28, 2026, and the largest single-day drop arrived the day after the company reported its third quarter. The decline looks like a bargain if Meta's ad sales keep growing, and like a warning if spending on data centers keeps running ahead of its cash. So has buying Meta stock after a fall this size paid off before?

What Happened After Meta Stock's Past Falls?

In most cases, buyers who held on for a year came out ahead. Between May 2012 and October 2026, Meta stock recorded seven falls of more than 20% over 30 trading days. Twelve months later, the stock was higher after five of those declines, and the median result was a 57.0% gain.

Buyers usually sat through a further drop first. In the median case, the stock's lowest close within a year was 25.8% below its price on the day of the dip. The year's highest price then arrived after a median of 308 days, or about ten months. The February 2022 fall went the other way: the stock never closed above its dip-day price within a year, and at its lowest was 62.6% below that mark.

Meta's Ad Sales Are Still Growing

Growth has eased slightly since earlier in the year. Meta's revenue rose 26.1% from a year earlier in the third quarter of fiscal 2026, compared with 28.0% in the second quarter. Management expects fourth-quarter revenue of $73 billion to $76 billion, up from $59.9 billion a year earlier.

Nearly all of Meta's revenue comes from ads. Sales of ads across the Family of Apps, which includes Facebook and Instagram, reached $63.1 billion in the third quarter, up 26%, management said. Advertisers paid 14% more per ad on average, an increase management partly attributed to better ad performance.

title: Etsy CEO has an unexpected message for shoppers
detail:
Etsy CEO has an unexpected message for shoppers
Moz Farooque
Wed, October 28, 2026 at 8:37 PM EDT 5 min read
ETSY
RDDT
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Say you're browsing through Etsy (ETSY) for a birthday gift and find the perfect hand-painted mug. The photos look beautiful, and the description on them offers a personal touch, while you're already picturing the smile when your cousin opens it.

However, with all the chaos from AI-generated imagery, it becomes incredibly tough to spot whether the item in the listing is really what will arrive at your door.

Those are no longer abstract questions for Etsy's shoppers, and the problem was best explained by Reddit user u/ZealousidealTowel229 in the r/Etsy community, who complained that searching for fall decor brought up what appeared to be AI-generated products from shops with barely any sales.

"I will never buy something I can't see what it is in reality," the user wrote.

That said, CEO Kruti Patel Goyal believes the answer isn't about retreating from artificial intelligence. In fact, it's more about using the technology to help customers find genuine craftspeople and products that feel personal.

That unexpected message comes at a point when Etsy's latest earnings show active buyers growing year over year for the first time in two years, with merchandise sales climbing 8.8%. The turnaround has caught Wall Street's attention, too, with Etsy's stock price surging nearly 28% this month.

To keep that momentum, Goyal will have to make good on a bigger promise: AI strengthening the very human connection Etsy shoppers value.

Etsy CEO Kruti Patel Goyal says AI could make shopping more human.grinvalds / Getty Images
Etsy CEO says AI could make handmade shopping more personal

Etsy has about 100 million listings, which means finding the perfect handmade gift can sometimes feel like searching for a needle in a haystack.

More Retail:

Kroger cuts discounts, promises pricing changes

Walmart gets aggressive when it comes to holiday sales

Costco copies a popular Trader Joe's collectible

CEO Kruti Patel Goyal believes AI can change that without taking away what makes Etsy special.

In her October 28 shareholder letter, she explained:

"There's an inherent paradox in how we think about AI at Etsy: we're harnessing technology to make commerce more human."

The idea is to use AI to help shoppers discover products that match their tastes while making the people behind those products more visible.

Etsy is already using machine learning to personalize recommendations and search results. Four out of five active buyers now have profiles powering personalized feeds and marketing.

Meanwhile, the company is testing ways to highlight sellers' stories, craftsmanship, and creative processes, giving shoppers a better sense of who they're buying from.

Reddit Fell 5% on Slower-Growth Fears. The October 29 Outlook Decides Whether the Multiple Holds ©cyano66 from Getty Images via Canva
Key Takeaways

Reddit shares fell 5% on Monday as worries about slowing growth weighed on the stock ahead of its third-quarter report on Oct. 29.

The fourth-quarter outlook matters more than the third-quarter beat, because it shows whether growth is slowing as gradually as analysts expect.

At 16x forward earnings, Reddit trades at the bottom of its one-year range, though analysts have raised their 2027 earnings estimate by 25% since the end of 2025.

Watch for a fourth-quarter revenue guide of about $1.05 billion and for U.S. daily users above the second quarter's 53.2 million.

Reddit (RDDT:NYSE) fell 5% on Monday as worries about slowing growth hung over its third-quarter report, due after the close on Thursday, Oct. 29. Snap fell 3% the same day and Meta barely moved, so the selling hit Reddit's own growth story hardest.

Reddit has beaten the top of its own revenue guidance by $58 million to $80 million in each of the last three quarters. Another third-quarter beat wouldn't surprise anyone. The fourth-quarter outlook is the number that decides whether the stock's multiple holds.

The slowdown is already in the guidance

When Reddit reported in July, it guided third-quarter revenue to $860 million to $870 million, up 47% to 49%. That's a step down from the second quarter, when revenue grew 61% to $805 million.

It also stopped reporting U.S. logged-in daily users as a separate number, after that figure grew just 1% in the second quarter, to 23.1 million.

Analysts expect the slowdown to keep going. Consensus calls for revenue of $3.39 billion in 2026, up 54% from 2025's $2.2 billion, then $4.47 billion in 2027 (up 32%) and $5.58 billion in 2028 (up 25%).

Reddit (RDDT): revenue, actual and consensus estimates, $ billions, fiscal 2024–2028 (TIKR)

To hit that 2026 figure, Reddit needs fourth-quarter revenue of roughly $1.05 billion to $1.06 billion, up about 45% from last year's $726 million. A guide in that range keeps the analysts' path intact. A guide below it would push analysts to cut their numbers, unless investors trust Reddit to beat its guide again the way it has all year.

The multiple already prices in a steeper slowdown

Even after Monday's drop, Reddit trades at 16x forward earnings. That's the lowest point of the past year, against an average of 26x and a high of 49x in mid-January.
